tapsOrSteps: About 71 taps in the e2e pass and 73 in the real-timing pass: 3 to reach Flashcards with Hard on (Drills tab, Flashcards, Hard chip), 60 answers, about 4 to visit Home midway, about 4 to reach Home and Stats at the end, plus 2-3 Stats tab taps. With human think time it took about 2.7 minutes (160.9s) in Chromium without ?e2e=1, and 73s with ?e2e=1. The drill part works and Hard reached 54/60 correct, but Home never tells the user that, and Stats needs 2-3 extra taps on collapsed sections before any Hard figure is visible.
narrative:
Fresh install. Home said "Learn basic strategy - Hard totals: 0 answers so far, 20 needed to judge. Get every category to 90%." That was clear. Flashcards is below the fold on the Drills picker, under five counting drills, so a beginner has to scroll for it. Opening Flashcards and tapping Hard worked, and every dealt hand was a real hard total.

I answered 60 cards: 6 deliberate misses early (beginner), then all right, ending at 54/60 = 90%. I checked every grade against my own copy of the 6D H17 DAS LS chart, which matches src/engine/charts/d68_h17.ts. All 60 grades agreed (including 17 v A = surrender and 9 v 7 = hit), and no soft hands or pairs leaked into Hard scope. The result strip was clear and quick: "Correct! 7,2 v 9 - Hit", or a red card with You played / Right play / Show on chart. The flashcard screen never shows progress toward the 20-answer / 90% goal, so the user drills blind.

After 30 answers (80%) I went to Home. Hard had disappeared from Next step. It now said "Soft totals: 0 answers so far", and the only mention of Hard was "weakest: hard totals". Tapping Start reopened Flashcards still set to Hard, not Soft. After 60 answers (90%, goal met), Home showed exactly the same Next step text and still said "weakest: hard totals". There was no confirmation that Hard was done.

Stats opens on the Play tab. A six-row CVCX/profile block of em-dashes fills the first screen, and without ?e2e=1 every useful section is collapsed. Once opened, "Accuracy by category" (on the Play tab, although it is fed by drills) and Drills > Flashcards both say Hard totals 54/59 (92%), while Flashcards overall says 54/60 = 90%. The surrender-cell miss was filed under Surrender, not Hard. Home's Next step uses the per-cell numbers, which give 54/60 = 90%. A seeded repro at the 90% line shows the two screens disagreeing: Home says "Hard totals are at 89%", Stats says "53/58 (91%)".

Reloading kept all progress. There were no console or page errors in Chromium or WebKit, no sideways scroll, and no clipped controls. The only targets under 44px are the 22x22 native checkboxes (Eyes-free audio, Voice answers, look-alike option).

findings.title: Home Start opens a different hand type from the one Next step names
findings.steps: Fresh install. Drills > Flashcards > Hard, answer 30 or more. Home now says 'Learn basic strategy - Soft totals: 0 answers so far, 20 needed to judge.' Tap Start.
findings.expected: Flashcards opens with Soft selected (the hand type Next step just named), or at least says the selection was changed.
findings.actual: Flashcards opens with the saved Hard-only selection (Hard=true, Soft=false), dealing hard hands. Answering more of them never moves the Next step forward. Same result after 60 answers.
findings.suggestedFix: Make NextStep carry the hand type it is about (for example scope: 'soft'), and pass it through setDrillLaunch. When Drills mounts with a flash launch, save withScopes(settings, [scope]) before mounting FlashcardsView. The same applies to 'Hard totals are at N%': launch on that hand type.

findings.title: Home and Stats give different Hard percentages, so they can disagree on whether the 90% goal is met
findings.steps: Drill Hard and miss a surrender cell (for example stand on 17 v A). Compare Home Next step with Stats > Accuracy by category, or Drills > Flashcards. Seeded repro: boundary.mjs.
findings.expected: One Hard-totals figure everywhere. The screen that sets the 90% goal and the screen that reports progress agree.
findings.actual: After the real run, Stats shows Hard totals 54/59 (92%) plus Surrender 0/1, while Next step counts 54/60 = 90%. At the line: Home says 'Hard totals are at 89%; get every category to 90%' while Stats says 'Hard totals 53/58 (91%)'. grade.ts files any hand whose right play is surrender under 'surrender'. Stats reads that stats.categories tally, but nextStep sums every hard-* cell in cellStats.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/Stats.tsx (Accuracy by category, Flashcards section), src/ui/screens/nextStep.ts, src/engine/grade.ts (category ~L279), src/ui/screens/readiness.ts
findings.suggestedFix: Have Stats' Hard/Soft/Pairs rows read the same hard-/soft-/pair- sums from cellStats that nextStep uses, through a shared helper (for example categoryFromCells). Keep Surrender as its own breakdown line. Use pctDown (floor) in both places so 89.8% never shows as 90% on one screen and 89% on the other.

findings.title: Home never shows progress on the hand type being drilled, and never confirms the goal is met
findings.steps: Drill Hard to 80% (30 answers) and visit Home. Drill on to 90% / 60 answers and visit Home again.
findings.expected: Something like 'Hard totals: 90% over 60 - done. Next: Soft totals'. The midway visit shows 'Hard 80%, 10 points to go'.
findings.actual: Next step jumps straight to 'Soft totals: 0 answers so far' as soon as Hard passes 20 answers, before Hard reaches 90%. The text is identical at 80% and at 90%. The only Hard mention is 'weakest: hard totals', still shown at 90%, which reads as a failure right when the goal was met. Hard below 90% is only named again once soft and pairs each have 20+ answers.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small three-row progress list to the Next step card (Hard / Soft / Pairs, each answers out of 20 and % against 90%, with a check when met). Let weakestCategories drop categories already at or above CATEGORY_TARGET, or label the line 'lowest'.

findings.title: Flashcards shows no progress toward the 20-answer / 90% goal
findings.steps: Drills > Flashcards > Hard, answer 60 cards.
findings.expected: A quiet line under the chips or above the action bar, for example 'Hard 47/52 - 90% (goal 90%, 20+)', and a one-time 'Hard totals on target' note when it crosses.
findings.actual: Only the per-card result strip. To know whether the goal is met, the user has to leave the drill (Back, then Home tab) and read Home, which does not report it either (see above).
findings.suggestedFix: Compute the selected hand types' cellStats totals with the nextStep helper and show one line in the empty space above the action bar. Show a short confirmation the first time a selected hand type crosses MIN_CATEGORY_ANSWERS and CATEGORY_TARGET.

findings.title: Stats opens on empty CVCX rows, and the useful sections start collapsed
findings.steps: After drilling, tap Home > All stats (without ?e2e=1).
findings.expected: The first screen answers 'how am I doing on the plays?'. Accuracy by category, or the drill tallies, is visible without extra taps.
findings.actual: The default Play tab's first screen is a six-row 'Profile: Default' block of em-dashes (CVCX score, EV, risk of ruin, sim note, play accuracy, units per hour). It is the only section open by default and repeats on the Drills and Progress tabs. Accuracy by category and Flashcards are collapsed below the fold. Accuracy by category, which is fed by Flashcards, sits on the Play tab. Seeing the Hard figure takes All stats, scroll, and tapping a collapsed header (or Drills tab, then Flashcards).
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse the Profile/CVCX block by default, or hide it when every value is empty, and show it only on Play. Open the first section that has data, or default Accuracy by category / Flashcards to open. Open Stats on the Drills tab when the user has no table sessions yet.

findings.title: Flashcards is below the fold on the Drills picker although Home sends beginners there first
findings.steps: Fresh install, tap the Drills tab.
findings.expected: The drill Home recommends (Flashcards, for basic strategy) is visible without scrolling, or highlighted.
findings.actual: Five counting drills come first. 'Knowing the plays > Flashcards' is cut off by the tab bar at 375x812.
findings.suggestedFix: Put 'Knowing the plays' first, or pin a 'Recommended: <Next step>' card at the top of the picker.

findings.title: Miss explanation repeats 'Basic' and does not explain the play
findings.steps: Answer 2,9 v 4 with Stand.
findings.expected: A short reason a beginner can learn from, for example 'Double 11 against everything: you're the favourite to draw a 10'.
findings.actual: 'Basic strategy error. Basic double vs dealer 4': the word Basic twice, and it only restates the answer.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the second 'Basic', or replace the reason with a one-line rule for that row (hard 12-16 v 2-6 stand, 11 double, and so on).

findings.title: Stats bars have no marker at the 90% target
findings.steps: Open Stats > Accuracy by category after drilling Hard to 90%.
findings.expected: The 90% target is drawn on the bar, or the row is marked as on target.
findings.actual: A plain green bar with no target. 89% and 92% look the same.
findings.suggestedFix: Draw a tick at CATEGORY_TARGET and add 'on target' when n >= MIN_CATEGORY_ANSWERS and pct >= target.

findings.title: Settings gear renders as a colour emoji in WebKit
findings.steps: Open Home in WebKit and compare with Chromium.
findings.expected: The same plain glyph in both.
findings.actual: WebKit draws the colour gear emoji next to 'Settings'; Chromium draws a plain glyph.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the U+FE0E text-style selector after the gear, or use an inline SVG icon.

topChanges: Make Home's Next step name a hand type and have Start open Flashcards on that type (save the selection on launch). Today Start reopens the old Hard-only selection while the card says Soft.
Use one Hard/Soft/Pairs tally everywhere: Stats should read the same cellStats sums as nextStep, so the 90% goal and the reported % agree (now 89% on Home vs 91% on Stats at the line).

Show progress against the goal: a Hard/Soft/Pairs answers-out-of-20 and %-against-90% list on Home's Next step card, a one-line counter plus a one-time 'on target' note in Flashcards, and drop 'weakest: hard totals' once Hard is at 90%.

tapsOrSteps: Happy path, 8 navigation taps plus answers: Drills tab, scroll, Speed (2 taps). Back, scroll, Mastery challenge (2 taps; resumed at 61/330). Long-press the hand, then Amber (2 gestures). Stats tab, Last 7 days (2 taps). The real-timing Chromium pass (no ?e2e=1) took 102 taps in 2.2 minutes: 60 Speed answers, 14 Mastery answers and 30 Stats range/tab taps. The Chromium e2e pass took 82 taps in 0.7 minutes, and WebKit e2e took 82 taps in 1.8 minutes. There were no console or page errors in any pass and no sideways scroll on any screen. Every Speed and Mastery button measured at least 44px; the marker swatches are exactly 44x44.
narrative:
Seed: 249 of the 330 cells have cellStats, about 80% of them dated in the last 7 days. Three cells are weak (12 v 3, A,7 v 9, 9,9 v 7). Also seeded: 380 dated latency rows, 11 count-drill runs, 14 true-count rows and 4 Play sessions over 3 weeks, a Mastery run at index 61, and a red marker on soft-18-v-9.

Home opened at 97% accuracy with "Next step: Fix weak cells (Hard 12 v 3 is at 50%)". Nothing on Home mentions the Mastery run that is 61/330 in progress.

Speed warm-up: 2 taps plus a long scroll (Speed is the 11th drill). It remembered Surrender. The yes/no loop is fast and clear. I checked every verdict (about 140 across passes) against src/engine/strategy, 6D H17 DAS LS, by hand: 16 v 9/10/A, 15 v 10/A and 17 v A surrender; 8,8 v A surrender; A,2 v 6 double; 11 v A double; 7,7 v 2 split. All correct. Problems with the warm-up:
- There is no clock and no session length, so a "5-minute warm-up" has to be timed by hand.
- Switching question mode wipes the score with no summary: 40 answers ended showing "10/11".
- Long-pressing the hand in Speed does nothing.

Mastery: resumed exactly at 61/330 · All. A 250ms press did not open the marker picker; a 700ms press opened "Marker for Pair of 10s vs 2". Amber put a dot on the hand without answering it and without moving progress. 14 correct answers took it to 75/330. Leaving to Home and coming back kept 75/330, and a reload kept progress too. A deliberate slip showed "Run reset at 3/330", and Wrong tap put it back to 3/330. That part works well.

Branch run: in Speed I narrowed Hands to Pairs for Split? practice. Opening Mastery then showed 0 / 100 · Pairs, and the 61/330 run was overwritten in storage. Tapping All only gave 0/330. The run is gone.

Stats: Last 7 and Last 30 days do change Table sessions (4 to 2), True count (11/14 to 7/9) and Fatigue (18 to 7 sessions). They do not change anything the user sees first. Accuracy by category, Flashcards (97%, 1777/1830), Mistake types and the I18 table are identical in every range, while the median-time line on the same rows does change. Speed's yes/no taps are also counted as Flashcards and per-cell decisions, which raised a weak cell to passing.

WebKit matched Chromium on Speed, the Mastery marker picker and Stats 7d.

findings.title: Changing Hands scope in Speed silently destroys the in-progress Mastery run
findings.steps: Seed a Mastery run at 61/330 (scope All). Open Drills > Speed and tap Pairs in the Hands row (Speed's own 'nothing to ask' copy tells users to 'Choose Pairs' for Split?). Answer a few. Back > Mastery challenge.
findings.expected: Mastery resumes at 61/330, or at least warns before discarding it. The scope Speed uses should not decide whether the sweep survives.
findings.actual: Mastery opens at '0 / 100 cleared · Pairs', and bjtrainer.masteryrun.v1 is overwritten on mount (index 0, 100 cells). Tapping All gives '0 / 330'; the 61-hand run is unrecoverable. No message at any point.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/drills/MasteryChallengeView.tsx (useState initialiser plus the saveMasteryRun effect); scopes shared via src/ui/screens/drills/HandDeckControls.tsx
findings.suggestedFix: Store the run's own scope/deck with the run, and on open restore that scope instead of starting fresh. Or keep runs keyed by universe (one per scope) and never overwrite the saved run until the user answers a hand in the new scope. At minimum show 'Your 61/330 All sweep is paused — switch back to All to continue'.

findings.title: Speed yes/no answers count as correct chart decisions and clear weak cells
findings.steps: Seed A,7 v 9 at 5/8 (62%, listed by Home as a weak cell). Speed > Double > Deck: Marked. Answer 'No' 6 times to 'Double?' on A,7 v 9.
findings.expected: A yes/no answer to 'Double?' says nothing about whether you hit or stand A,7 v 9 (the actual confusion). It should not move the cell's accuracy, Flashcards %, or Home's weak-cell list, or it should be tracked separately.
findings.actual: cellStats soft-18-v-9 went from 5/8 to 11/14 (79%). Home's Next step went from 'Hard 12 v 3 … and 2 more cells' to '… and 1 more cell': the weak cell was cleared without ever being played. The Stats 'Flashcards' section also gained a 'Surrender 6/6' row and its total rose by Speed's taps. 'Accuracy by category > Surrender' median decision time is now entirely yes/no taps (0.4s/1.3s).
findings.likelyFile: src/drills/speedDrill.ts (SPEED_EVENT_SOURCE = 'flashcard', buildSpeedEvent hand: cellId); src/drills/gradeAnswer.ts persistGrade/applyEvents
findings.suggestedFix: Give Speed its own source (or a flag on the event) and skip cellStats/bySource.flashcard/latencyHistory for it. Or record only Speed misses against the cell, since a miss is real evidence and a correct 'No' is not.

findings.title: Stats time filter leaves every hand-accuracy figure unchanged; same rows mix all-time accuracy with ranged median time
findings.steps: Returning user with most answers in the last 7 days and some 9–20 days ago. Stats > Play (or Drills) > tap Last 7 days, then Last 30 days.
findings.expected: 'Am I better than last week?': hand accuracy for the selected range.
findings.actual: Everything above the fold is identical in all ranges: Profile/CVCX block, Accuracy by category (Hard 755/774), Flashcards (97%, 1777/1830), Mistake types, I18 table. Only the 'Median decision time' line under each category changes (Pairs 1.8s to 1.5s), so a single row shows all-time accuracy next to last-7-days time. The note lists only 'Accuracy by category and the Illustrious 18 table' as all-time; Flashcards and Mistake types are not mentioned but also ignore the range. To a user, tapping Last 7 days looks like it did nothing.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/Stats.tsx (categories/bySource read unfiltered); src/store/types.ts latencyHistory row lacks `correct`
findings.suggestedFix: Add `correct: boolean` to each dated latencyHistory row (already one per timed graded event) and compute ranged per-category accuracy from it. Until then, grey out or badge 'all time' on each unfiltered section (Flashcards and Mistake types too). Move range-sensitive sections above the CVCX block.

findings.title: Speed has no clock or session length and mode switches wipe the score with no summary
findings.steps: Open Speed for a '5-minute warm-up'. Answer 16 Surrender questions, switch to Double, answer 13, switch to Split, answer 11.
findings.expected: The drill is described as 'Yes or no, against the clock'. A warm-up wants a visible timer or a set length, and a session total that survives switching question type.
findings.actual: There is no timer, countdown or end screen. Each mode tap silently resets to '0/0 –', so after 40 answers the header showed '10/11 0.4s' (real pass: 60 answers showed '27/31'). The second number has no label (it is a median). There is no way to see the whole warm-up's result except in Stats.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/drills/SpeedDrillView.tsx (sessionKey effect resets score; topbar speed-stats)
findings.suggestedFix: Add an optional 2/5-minute timer chip with an end card (answers, accuracy, median, misses to review). Keep a running session total across mode changes, with a per-mode breakdown. Label the median ('median 1.5s').

findings.title: Home does not mention a Mastery sweep in progress
findings.steps: Seed a Mastery run at 61/330 plus a few weak cells; open the app.
findings.expected: A returning user sees 'Resume Mastery: 61/330' (one tap) somewhere on Home.
findings.actual: Next step says 'Fix weak cells'. Nothing on Home shows or links to the 61/330 run, so resuming takes Drills > scroll past 10 entries > Mastery.
findings.suggestedFix: When loadMasteryRun() has 0 < index < order.length, show a 'Continue sweep 61/330' row (or Next-step secondary button) that uses setDrillLaunch('mastery').

findings.title: Long-press marking does nothing in Speed (or anywhere outside Flashcards/Mastery), and nothing hints it exists
findings.steps: In Speed, hold the player's hand for 700ms.
findings.expected: Either the marker picker opens (as in Mastery), or long-press is clearly scoped. Some hint that hands can be marked.
findings.actual: Nothing happens (0 dialogs). In Mastery it works, but no on-screen hint mentions long-press, so the feature is only discoverable by accident.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap Speed's hand-cards in MarkableHand (handKey = idRef/question). Add a one-time 'Hold a hand to mark it' hint under the hand.

findings.title: Speed 'Split?' on 8,8 v A answers No with 'Chart: Surrender' and no fallback
findings.steps: Speed > Split (scope All). When 8,8 v A is dealt, answer Yes.
findings.expected: Correct for 6D H17 LS, but the reason should say why: 'Chart: Surrender (split if surrender isn't offered)'.
findings.actual: judgeSpeed('split', 8,8, A) gives answer No, reason 'Chart: Surrender'. A learner who split is told 'No', which reads as 'don't split 8s'.
findings.suggestedFix: When basic is surrender and the mode asks split/double, add the no-surrender fallback (from fallbackHand) to the reason line.

findings.title: Home profile chip slides under the mute disc when scrolled
findings.steps: Home with a seeded history (page is 44px taller than 812). Scroll to the bottom.
findings.expected: Header controls stay clear of the fixed mute disc.
findings.actual: Profile chip rect [196,24,352,72] overlaps the mute disc [323,0,367,44] by about 29x20px. The chip text 'Default (6D H17)' is partly covered.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the same mute-disc clearance used for the Stats/Settings headers to .home-head (right padding = disc width + gap), or make the header sticky below the safe area like the drill topbars.

findings.title: Profile/CVCX block of dashes leads every Stats tab, pushing range-sensitive content below the fold
findings.steps: Stats > Drills or Progress tab, any range.
findings.expected: The first screen shows the data for the selected tab and range.
findings.actual: Six rows of 'CVCX … —' occupy most of the first screen on all three tabs. The first content that answers the range picker starts around 700px down.
findings.suggestedFix: Show the Profile/CVCX block only on the Play tab, collapsed by default when every value is empty.

topChanges: Stop the Mastery run being destroyed by scope changes made in other drills: persist the run's own scope/deck and restore it on open (or keep one saved run per scope), and never overwrite the saved run until a hand is answered in the new scope.
Keep Speed's yes/no taps out of per-cell accuracy, Flashcards totals and category decision times (own event source, or record misses only), so a warm-up cannot clear weak cells or inflate the 97%.

Make the Stats time range answer the user's real question: add `correct` to dated latencyHistory rows and filter hand accuracy by range, badge any section still on all time, and move ranged sections above the CVCX block. Also add a Speed session timer with an end card, plus a 'Continue sweep 61/330' row on Home.

tapsOrSteps: Story path from the real 40-card state: Home Start (1 tap), 40 answers, Stats tab plus expanding Cost of mistakes (2), then Drills > Custom > Auto > Flashcards (4) to reach the first Focus card, 40 more answers, Back > Custom > Auto > Mastery (4). Home never sends this player to Custom. I kept obeying Next step for 360 answers (about 370 taps) and it still said 'Learn basic strategy'. In a seeded 'a few sessions in' state (categories at 90% or better, 6 weak cells), Next step says 'Fix weak cells': Start > Flashcards is 2 taps to the first Focus card. It took 120 correct answers (95 of them on Focus cells, about 10 minutes at a real pace) before Home moved on to 'Mastery sweep'. 71 screenshots, Chromium plus a WebKit repeat, about 20 browser runs, no console or page errors.
narrative:
Fresh install, Default 6D H17. Home's Next step 'Learn basic strategy' > Start opened Flashcards straight away. I answered 40 cards, deliberately missing every soft double and splits of 2s, 3s, 4s, 6s, 7s and 9s, and got everything else right: 9 misses, 78% overall. Every verdict matched src/engine (correctPlay). I also checked the Custom grid's H17/DAS/LS chart cells by eye and they were right.

Back on Home, Next step said 'Pairs: 10 answers so far, 20 needed', and Start opens the same plain all-chart Flashcards. Stats > Cost of mistakes lists '9,9 v 6: Stand for Split x1, 0.20 u' and the rest. But the section sits only on the Play tab, even though every priced mistake came from Flashcards. It is collapsed by default, and its rows look tappable but do nothing. There is no way from 'this is costing you' to 'drill this'.

To test whether Home ever closes the loop on its own, I kept obeying Next step in batches of 40, still missing the same plays, up to 360 answers. It never left 'Learn basic strategy' (soft 59%, pairs 49%): the category-at-90% step comes before 'Fix weak cells', so the exact weakness Custom is built to fix keeps it out of reach. Plain Flashcards also re-drew my previously missed cells only 1-7 times per 40 cards while unseen cells remained. An unseen card weighs 8 and a just-missed card weighs 6.

Doing what a user would do, I went to Drills > Custom by hand and tapped Auto. It correctly painted exactly my 9 missed cells Focus. The only feedback is a small '9 Focus · 290 Regular · 31 Rare' line, and the grid is about 900px further down. In Custom Flashcards, Focus cells were 8 of the first 20 draws but only 4 of the next 20 (30% against the 60% mix). Each Focus cell drops to an SR weight of 0.25 after one right answer, while the 290 unseen Regular cells stay at 8.

Mastery from Custom is a 330-hand sweep, because Auto paints every cell. None of the first 12 hands were Focus cells, and one soft-double miss reset the run at 16/330.

Separately, Custom edits are never saved until a Start button is tapped. Auto plus a painted-Off row read 'null' in localStorage, and after a relaunch the editor showed '0 Focus · 330 Regular'. That matters for an iOS home-screen app that gets evicted.

In the seeded state the intended path works: Next step 'Fix weak cells - 2,2 v 3 is at 33% and 5 more cells below 78%' > Start opens Custom with Auto already applied (exactly the 6 seeded cells) > Flashcards drew Focus cells 79% of the time. Closing the loop still took 120 answers, because accuracy is all-time and a 2/6 cell needs about 13 right in a row, and nothing in the drill shows progress. Afterwards Home said 'Mastery sweep', but its Start opened Mastery still on the leftover 'Custom' deck. Without e2e mode the timings felt fine (next card ready 25-435 ms after a tap). WebKit rendered the three key screens the same as Chromium.

findings.title: Home Next step never routes a concentrated weakness to 'Fix weak cells'
findings.steps: Fresh install > Next step Start > answer flashcards, missing every soft double and splits of 2/3/4/6/7/9s (everything else right) > after each batch of 40, go back Home and tap Next step Start again. Continue to 360 answers.
findings.expected: Once specific cells are clearly weak (here: 9,9 v 5/6/8, 6,6 v 2/3, A,2-A,7 doubles), Next step points to Custom with Auto, the tool built for this, or at least to the weak category.
findings.actual: Next step stayed 'Learn basic strategy' for all 360 answers ('Soft totals are at 68%' ... 'Pairs are at 49%'). Start always opened all-chart Flashcards. Weak cells with 5 or more answers existed from answer 320, but step 2 (custom) cannot fire while step 1 (every category at 90%) fails, and a concentrated weakness keeps its category below 90%.
findings.suggestedFix: In nextStep(), once a category has at least MIN_CATEGORY_ANSWERS but is below target, check for weak cells in that category (allow MIN_CELL_ANSWERS of 2-3, or 'missed and due') and return kind 'custom' with those cells named. Keep 'flash' only for the too-few-answers case. Alternatively, have 'flash' Start open Flashcards scoped to the weak category instead of All.

findings.title: Custom editor edits (Auto, paint, mix, Favour missed) are not saved until a Start button is tapped
findings.steps: Drills > Custom > tap Auto (11 Focus) > choose the Off brush and tap the A,9 row (10 Off) > reload or relaunch the app (as iOS does when it evicts the home-screen PWA) > Drills > Custom.
findings.expected: The painted selection and Auto tiers are still there.
findings.actual: After relaunch: '0 Focus · 330 Regular · 0 Rare · 0 Off'. localStorage bjtrainer.settings.v1 drill.custom was null before the reload. CustomDrillEditor.commit only calls onSettingsChange, which Drills receives as App's setSettings (memory only). Only onStart calls saveSettings. The harness used by the editor spec does call saveSettings, so no test can catch this.
findings.suggestedFix: Call saveSettings(next) inside CustomDrillEditor.commit (as customDrillEditor.harness.tsx does), or give Drills a persisting onSettingsChange. Add an e2e test that paints, reloads and re-opens via the real app, not the harness.

findings.title: Missed cells are drawn less often than unseen cells in Flashcards and in Mastery order
findings.steps: Answer flashcards on the Chart deck, missing some cells. Track how often previously missed cells come back while most cells are still unseen. Also start Mastery from Custom after Auto.
findings.expected: A just-missed cell comes back soon and more often than a never-seen one, as the Mastery copy says ('due and missed cells come first').
findings.actual: srWeight gives an unseen card 8 but a just-missed card only 6 (box 0: 1 + 0 + 5). Batches of 40 drew previously missed cells 1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 5 times while about half the chart was unseen. In Mastery from Custom, none of the first 12 cells were Focus (missed) cells. In the seeded state, 1 of the first 15.
findings.suggestedFix: Make a box-0 missed card outweigh an unseen one, e.g. add a recent-miss bonus so box 0 with reviews > 0 weighs at least 2x SR_NEW_WEIGHT. When Mastery runs on a Custom deck, multiply its order weights by the Custom tier weights.

findings.title: Custom Focus share collapses after one correct answer when most cells are unseen
findings.steps: From the 40-answer state: Drills > Custom > Auto (9 Focus, 290 Regular, 31 Rare, mix 60/30/10) > Flashcards > answer 40 correctly.
findings.expected: About 60% of draws come from the 9 Focus cells until they are fixed.
findings.actual: Focus draws were 8 of the first 20, then 4 of the next 20 (12/40 = 30%). After one right answer a Focus cell's SR weight drops from 6 to 0.25 while each unseen Regular cell stays at 8, so the tier share is swamped. Every Focus cell was still at 1/2 = 50% after the session.
findings.suggestedFix: Normalise SR weights within each tier before applying the tier share, so tiers keep their advertised percentages and SR only orders cells within a tier. Or floor the SR weight of Focus cells at 1.

findings.title: Cost of mistakes is a dead end: inert rows, Play tab only, collapsed by default, labels don't match the grid

findings.title: The leftover Custom deck carries into Home's other next steps

findings.expected: Home's 'Learn basic strategy' and 'answer every cell once' steps open on the whole chart.
findings.actual: Both opened with DECK: Custom. Flashcards kept drawing from the old Auto tiers. Mastery showed '0 / 330 cleared · Custom · All'. A whole-chart sweep only counts when all 330 cells are in the run (isWholeChartSweep), so any Off-painted cell makes Home's Mastery step impossible to complete from its own Start button.

findings.title: Closing the loop takes about 13 straight right answers per weak cell, with no progress shown
findings.steps: Seeded: 6 cells at 2/6 and everything else strong > Home 'Fix weak cells' > Start > Flashcards > answer correctly until Home changes.
findings.expected: Fixing a cell shows up soon, and the drill tells you how many weak cells are left and when you're done.
findings.actual: It took 120 answers (95 on Focus cells). Weak detection uses all-time accuracy, so (2+k)/(6+k) >= 78% needs k >= 13. The drill shows no 'weak cells left' count and no done state. The user has to go back to Home to find out.
findings.suggestedFix: Judge weak cells on recent answers (e.g. the last 5, or an EWMA) for both Auto and Next step. Show 'Focus cells left: N' in Custom-launched drills, with a done banner that sends you back to Home.

findings.title: Mastery from Custom sweeps all 330 hands, not the weak ones
findings.steps: Custom > Auto > Mastery.
findings.expected: Following the picker copy ('drill just those in Flashcards, Mastery or Mixed'), Mastery from Custom proves the Focus cells.

findings.title: Auto gives almost no visible feedback, and Back from Custom drills skips the editor
findings.steps: Custom > tap Auto. Then start Flashcards and tap Back.
findings.expected: Auto confirms what it did (e.g. 'Focus: 9,9 v 5, 9,9 v 6, ... 9 cells'). Back returns to the Custom editor you came from.

Back from Custom Flashcards or Mastery lands on the Drills picker, so re-checking or re-applying Auto costs an extra tap. The grid's 26x30 px cells and 26x28 px dealer headers are under 44px, and while scrolling the mute disc sits over the top-right grid cells.
findings.suggestedFix: After Auto, show an inline note naming the Focus cells, or scroll the first one into view. Remember that a drill was started from Custom and return there on Back.

findings.title: A lit Surrender button on pairs gives away 8,8 v A
findings.steps: Flashcards or Mastery: on most pair and soft hands Surrender is greyed and the chip says 'No surrender'. On 8,8 v A (H17 6D) Surrender lights up.
findings.expected: Button availability doesn't reveal the answer.
findings.actual: Of the pairs, only 8,8 v A lights Surrender (drillOffersSurrender follows the chart cell), so the button itself tells you the answer on that hand. The 'No surrender' chip on soft hands also contradicts a table that offers late surrender.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Surrender on every pair whenever the table has late surrender (taking it is a graded mistake), or at least on every pair vs 9/10/A, so it no longer singles out the one correct cell.

topChanges: Let Home's Next step send a player with concentrated misses straight to Custom (Auto) with the cells named. Today a below-90% category blocks the 'Fix weak cells' step forever, so plain all-chart Flashcards is the only advice (360 answers, never routed).

Save Custom editor changes on every commit, and when Home launches Flashcards or Mastery, reset the deck to Chart. Today Auto and paint are lost on relaunch until Start is tapped, and Home's next steps inherit a stale Custom deck.

Make weak cells actually come first. A just-missed card should outweigh an unseen one (today 6 vs 8). Custom tier shares should hold after one right answer (today Focus fell from 40% to 20% of draws). Mastery on Custom should walk the Focus cells first or only. Also give Cost of mistakes a 'Drill these' button and show it on the Drills tab.

tapsOrSteps: Getting into each piece takes about 8 navigation taps. Charts index list: Charts (1 tap), then a long scroll of about 1,800px with no jump link, then tap a corner-marked cell (1). Deviation quiz: Drills (1), scroll, Deviation quiz (1). Flashcards with count: Drills, Flashcards, Options, With count (4). One full loop (miss, explanation, Show on chart, Back to hand) is 3 taps. A human would need about 4-6 minutes for the whole story, plus drilling time. Scripted runs: 14 quiz answers with 4 misses and 3 chart round trips took 14 taps and 18.5s at real timing (no ?e2e=1). About 165 graded answers across Chromium and WebKit, and 85 screenshots.
narrative:
I played an intermediate player learning the Illustrious 18 on the default 6-deck H17 DAS LS profile.

Charts: the corner marks and inline notes are clear. Tapping 12 v 4 shows "12 v 4 · TC ≤ −1 · Hit". Tapping 16 v 10 adds the line that surrender comes first. The 10,10 indexes sit on the 18+ row and the note says "10,10 v 5", which makes sense once tapped. The Indexes table is correct and readable, but it is a dead end: it sits about 1,800px down the page, no row links to its cell or to a drill, and nothing tells you that you can drill these.

Advice is correct. Every graded item matched an independent oracle I wrote from the published Hi-Lo indexes (stand at index or above, hit below). That covered the H17 changes (10vA +3, 16v9 +4, 11vA always double), all the negative indexes, and the BJA H17 chart in docs/sources, which I read. The one cell I could not source is 12v6 under H17 (more below).

Deviation quiz: answering advances at once, and the last result sits as a strip under the next hand. The strip gives the play, the class (Missed / Phantom / Wrong either way) and the index label. "Show on chart" opens the chart over the drill with the cell ringed, plus a note when the chart and the grade differ ("This chart is basic strategy. That hand was graded double at a true count of +3…"). "Back to hand" returns to the same pending item, so nothing is lost. A miss comes back through spaced repetition: a missed TTv6 returned 8 items later. With one index picked from the Index list, the very next item was the same hand, which works as a retry. Picking an index has a catch: its full label, answer included, stays printed at the top of the screen.

Flashcards with count: the toggle is hidden under Options. On the default Chart deck only 1 hand in 40 involved an index, so for learning deviations it is basic strategy with a number on top. The Indexes deck works better. But on index cells where the count hasn't reached the index, the strip says "No index here", which contradicts the chart's corner mark. And Options has to be open to switch With count on, which makes the screen overflow: after an index miss the Hit/Stand/Double bar is pushed entirely off-screen at 375x812 (same in WebKit).

Stats has a per-index Right/Wrong table. Home still says "NEXT STEP: Learn basic strategy" and "weakest: hard totals" after 42 deviation answers. No console or page errors in any run.

findings.title: With Options open, a miss pushes the answer bar off-screen (Flashcards fully, quiz partly)
findings.steps: 375x812, Chromium or WebKit. Drills > Flashcards > Options > With count (Options stays open). Answer an index hand wrongly, e.g. 9,3 v 6 at TC -4 and tap Stand.
findings.expected: Hit/Stand/Double for the next card stay visible at the bottom; the strip shrinks or scrolls inside.
findings.actual: The page grows to 888px and the action bar sits at y=820-888, fully below the 812px viewport. You must scroll to answer the next card. In one run the page scrolled itself 76px instead, which pushed Back/Repeat under the mute disc. In the Deviation quiz with Options open, the bar is cut off by 19px and the page creeps 0 > 8 > 17px between items. The With count user always hits this, because the toggle lives inside Options.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/Drills.tsx (drill-screen layout, .action-bar is position: static) / src/ui/app.css
findings.suggestedFix: Make .action-bar position: sticky; bottom: 0 (or let the hand area flex-shrink with min-height: 0) so the drill screen never exceeds 100dvh. Also close the Options disclosure after a chip is toggled.

findings.title: With count says 'No index here' on index cells when the count hasn't reached the index
findings.steps: Flashcards > Deck: Indexes (With count on). Answer 4,8 v 2 at TC +0 with Hit, or 10,10 v 6 at TC +3 with Stand.
findings.expected: Something like 'Index not reached: 12 v 2 stands at TC ≥ +3', the way the Deviation quiz always prints the label.
findings.actual: 'Correct! 4,8 v 2 at TC +0 — Hit / No index here'. Same for 10,10 v 6 at +3, one count short of its +4 index, and for 12v4, 13v2, 9v7, 10v10 below their indexes. This tells a learner the cell has no index while the chart shows a corner mark on it.
findings.suggestedFix: In indexLine, when advice.deviationId is empty, call reachableIndexes(cards, up, ctx, rules). If any exist, return 'Index not reached: <label>'. Keep 'No index here' for cells with none.

findings.title: With count on the default Chart deck almost never asks an index (1 hand in 40)
findings.steps: Flashcards, Deck = Chart, Options > With count. Play 40 cards.
findings.expected: Enough index hands that 'With count' actually trains deviations, or a hint pointing to the Indexes deck.
findings.actual: Only 1 of 40 cards (4,5 v 7 at +5) involved an index. INDEX_SHARE only biases the count once a hand is dealt; it does not deal more index hands, and those are about 16 of roughly 270 cells. The Chart/Custom/Indexes/Marked deck list sits right next to the toggle with no explanation of how they combine.
findings.suggestedFix: When With count is on, weight the draw toward index cells (e.g. 30-40%), or show a hint under the chip: 'For index practice pick Deck: Indexes.'

findings.title: Picking one index in the quiz shows its answer above every question
findings.steps: Deviation quiz > Index list > pick '9 v 2: double at TC ≥ +1'. Drill.
findings.expected: The closed list shows only '9 v 2', so recall is still tested.
findings.actual: '9 v 2: double at TC ≥ +1' stays in the list box at the top of the screen for every question, which turns focused practice into reading.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/Drills.tsx (quiz-index-select options use the full Deviation.label)
findings.suggestedFix: Use a short option text (e.g. '9 v 2 (double)', without the threshold), or a custom button-list picker that shows only the hand.

findings.title: Indexes table and Stats index table are dead ends: no link to drill an index
findings.steps: Charts > scroll to Indexes, or Stats > Illustrious 18. Try to practise one row.
findings.expected: Tapping a row opens the Deviation quiz with that index picked (or highlights its cell).
findings.actual: Rows are plain text. Reaching the list means scrolling about 1,800px with no jump link, then 4 more taps and a manual pick from the list to drill it. Stats lists right/wrong per index, but you cannot drill the weakest one from there.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each index row a button that launches the quiz with quizIndex set. Add an 'Indexes ↓' jump link in the charts intro text.

findings.title: TC shows an ASCII hyphen next to the true minus sign in the same strip (quiz and flashcards)
findings.steps: Deviation quiz: answer a negative-count item wrongly.
findings.expected: One minus sign throughout, U+2212 as the index labels use.
findings.actual: '7,5 v 5 at TC -2' (ASCII) sits beside 'hit at TC ≤ −3' (U+2212), and the big 'TC -2' headline is ASCII too. This goes beyond the known peek/bet-or-sit/pair-cancel list: formatSigned is duplicated in 11 files (Drills.tsx, MistakeCard.tsx, handResult.ts, Stats.tsx, Table.tsx, ...).
findings.suggestedFix: Move formatSigned into one shared helper that returns '−' + Math.abs(n), and import it everywhere.

findings.title: Index miss card prints the same index line twice
findings.steps: Flashcards with count: miss an index hand (e.g. 4,5 v 7 at +5, Hit).
findings.expected: The index label appears once.
findings.actual: 'Index: 9 v 7: double at TC ≥ +3' then 'Missed deviation. 9 v 7: double at TC ≥ +3'. The extra line also adds height that feeds the overflow finding above.
findings.suggestedFix: Skip indexNote when the miss class is missed or phantom deviation, since the reason line already names the index.

findings.title: Index cells are 26x32px touch targets and the chart's dealer header row scrolls away
findings.steps: Charts > tap 12 v 4, or open Show on chart from a miss that adds the sticky explanation note.
findings.expected: 44px targets, or a list alternative; the dealer column header stays visible.
findings.actual: Cells are 26x32 (necessary to fit 10 columns, but under 44). With the sticky note, the DEALER 2..A header row is hidden, so you work out the column of the ringed cell from its position.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the chart thead sticky under the topbar and note. The tappable index rows suggested above also give a 44px way in.

findings.title: H17 12 v 6 threshold (hit at TC ≤ −3) is not covered by the repo's own source check
findings.steps: Compare src/engine/deviations.ts 12v6 with docs/sources/verified-surrender-indices.md section 6.

findings.actual: Commit 550b632 moved S17 12v6 from −1 to −2 but left H17 at −3. BJA_H17.pdf has no 12 v 6 entry, and the 5-for-5 table only checks the S17 value. If −3 was a published 'stand at ≥ −3' number, H17 should be ≤ −4. I could not find a source either way. Every other graded item matched my oracle.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask Jack to check his H17 source for 12 v 6 and record it in docs/sources like the 13 v 2 check. Change nothing without a source.

findings.title: WebKit: quiz Index list and checkboxes render with native styling (grey box, serif font)

findings.title: Home keeps prescribing basic strategy and calls hard totals the weakest after a deviation miss
findings.steps: Fresh profile; answer 42 Deviation quiz items with 1 missed deviation; go Home.
findings.expected: Next step acknowledges index practice (e.g. 'Indexes: 41/42'), or deviation misses aren't counted as hard-total weakness.
findings.actual: '98% · weakest: hard totals' and 'NEXT STEP Learn basic strategy — Soft totals: 0 answers'. Quiz items land in the Hard totals category, so one missed deviation shows up as a hard-totals weakness. An intermediate player gets no credit for index work.

findings.suggestedFix: Leave deviation-quiz events out of the basic category 'weakest' pick, or add an Indexes line and step to the Home card.

topChanges: Stop the answer bar being pushed off-screen: make .action-bar sticky to the bottom (or let the hand area shrink) and close Options after a chip is toggled. With count users hit this on their first miss.

Fix With count teaching: replace 'No index here' on index cells with 'Index not reached: <label>' (via reachableIndexes), and weight With count draws toward index cells or point users to Deck: Indexes.

tapsOrSteps: About 30 taps and roughly 3 minutes of real use for the core story. Home > Settings (1), Bone & Ink (1), speech rate +/+ and volume - (3), Audio detail: Verbosity Full and Answer pause + (3), Charts tab (1), Lowest first (1), indexed cell (1), gear (1), decks 2 / S17 / LS off (3), Done (1), Drills tab (1), gear (1), shot clock 5s (1), Done (1), Flashcards and 4 answers (5), Play tab (1), gear (1), Done (1), End x2 (2), Stats (1). The AMOLED and Slate passes took about 20 taps each (Settings > theme > every tab and every gear sheet). 99 screenshots in total, across Chromium e2e, Chromium with real timings, and WebKit.
narrative:
I started fresh on Midnight Felt, opened Settings from Home and picked Bone & Ink. The theme applies at once, survives a reload, and each picker card says what the theme is for, which helps. Speech rate, volume, verbosity and answer pause all changed and stuck. I didn't touch the Voice select or Test audio because both speak. Turning Audio off greys out the steppers properly.

On Charts in Bone the grids read well. No text failed WCAG in my automated sweep, except one tiny label on Play (below). Lowest first flipped every section and persisted. Tapping a corner-marked cell opened its index note inline. In the gear sheet I set 2 decks, S17 and no surrender. The ruleset line and the grids redrew straight away, and I checked every cell against 2D S17 DAS no-surrender basic strategy: hard, soft and pairs are all correct. The 6D H17 LS chart before the change was also correct (8,8 v A Rp, 11 v A Dh, A,8 v 6 Ds, 15/16/17 surrenders). Flashcard grading was correct too (10 v 5 Double, 13 v 10 Hit, A,9 v 7 Stand, 2,2 v 3 Split, A,A v 7 Split).

The Drills gear set the shot clock to 5s, and Flashcards used it. The Play gear sheet shows Training/Test, deal speed and the new-shoe group. Stats and the session report also render cleanly in Bone. AMOLED and Slate look consistent across every tab and sheet. I found no sideways scroll on any screen and no console or page errors in any run.

The story succeeds, but daylight readability has three real gaps. In Bone you can't tell which tab you're on: the active tab's colour has almost the same luminance as the others. Segmented controls in every theme mark the selected option only by text colour on a near-identical background. And the profile chip keeps saying 'Default (6D H17)' after the rules became 2D S17, so Home, Play, Stats and the sheet all show a label the chart contradicts.

The shot clock has two side effects. In visual mode it starts the next card while you're still reading the correction. And it auto-grades forever if you walk away: about 6 misses in 31 seconds, and Stats showed Hard 0/8 and Pairs 0/7 from nothing but idle time.

Smaller issues:
- One dark-green frame paints before Bone applies on cold load.
- The status bar is black-translucent (white clock and battery text) over a cream band in Bone. This is inferred from the meta tag; I didn't see it on a device.
- The gear renders as a colour emoji in WebKit.
- The Charts topbar wraps both the back label and the title to two lines.
- The deck buttons in the Charts sheet are 30-33px wide.

findings.title: Bone & Ink: the active tab can't be told apart from the others
findings.steps: Settings > Bone & Ink > tap Charts (or any tab) > look at the bottom tab bar
findings.expected: The current tab is obviously marked (higher contrast, weight or a fill), as in the dark themes where it turns gold or copper
findings.actual: Active tab colour is rgb(130,84,26) and inactive is rgb(95,85,70). Luminance is nearly identical, with the same weight and no background, so in shots 111 and 007 the Charts tab looks exactly like the others. Dark themes are fine (AMOLED gold 242,193,78 against grey 139,139,147).
findings.suggestedFix: Give .tab-btn-active a second cue that doesn't depend on hue, such as font-weight 700, a 3px top indicator bar or a tinted pill behind the glyph. Darken Bone's inactive tab colour toward a lighter grey so the active accent stands out (aim for 3:1 between active and inactive).

findings.title: Segmented controls mark the selected option only by text colour, in every theme
findings.steps: Open any gear sheet (Charts: Decks / Dealer soft 17; Drills: Shot clock; Play: Feedback / Count checks ask), or Settings > Verbosity / The two wheel buttons, in Bone, AMOLED or Slate
findings.expected: The selected option is unmistakable at a glance in daylight or glare, and styled like the Row order toggle on the same Charts screen (filled pill)
findings.actual: .segmented-btn-active only switches to background var(--raised) and colour var(--accent). In Bone the selected '2' / 'S17' / '5s' / 'Training' is near-white with brown text, while the unselected options are bone with darker text, so the selection reads weaker than the options around it. In AMOLED and Slate only the label hue changes. The Row order toggle a few pixels away uses a solid accent fill, so two selected-state styles sit side by side.
findings.suggestedFix: Match .charts-order-btn-active: background var(--accent), colour var(--accent-ink or --bg), font-weight 700. One selected-state style for every toggle in the app.

findings.title: Profile label says '6D H17' after the Charts gear changed the rules to 2D S17
findings.steps: Charts > gear > Decks 2, S17, LS off > Done > go to Home, Play, Stats, or reopen the gear
findings.expected: The label shown with the rules matches the rules in use, or the sheet warns that it's editing a profile whose name states different rules
findings.actual: Home chip, Play topbar ('Default (6D H17)' under Bankroll), Stats ('Profile: Default (6D H17)') and the sheet's own line ('Default (6D H17)'s rules') all keep saying 6D H17, while the chart header says '2 deck · S17 · DAS · No surrender' and the Play sheet says 'a 2-deck shoe'. A user studying in daylight sees two contradictory rule sets on one screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Don't bake rules into the default profile's name: call it 'Default' and render the live rulesetSummary beside it. At minimum, when ChartsSheet edits a profile whose name contains a rules token, rename it or show the live rules in the chip.

findings.title: Shot clock keeps grading misses forever when nobody is there, polluting stats
findings.steps: Drills gear > Shot clock 5s > Flashcards > put the phone down for 31 s > open Stats
findings.expected: After one or two timeouts in a row the drill pauses ('Still there? Tap to resume') and stops recording misses
findings.actual: 7 distinct cards went by in 31 s with no taps, and each timeout was graded as a miss and sent back to review now. Stats then showed Hard totals 0/8 and Pairs 0/7 with a median decision time of 5.0s, built from idle time alone. In a car, a traffic-light glance away does the same.
findings.suggestedFix: Count consecutive timeouts. After 2, stop auto-advancing and show a resume prompt. Exclude the idle run from latency medians, or record only the first timeout.

findings.title: In visual mode the shot clock starts the next card while the wrong-answer correction is still being read
findings.steps: Shot clock 5s (or 3s) > Flashcards > answer wrong > read the 'Wrong · You played / Right play / Basic strategy error' strip
findings.expected: The time spent reading a correction doesn't count against the next hand. The clock starts when the user dismisses the strip, or after a short reading grace.
findings.actual: The next card is dealt and its clock armed the moment you answer. 250 ms later the bar is already about 95% and draining under a 3-4 line correction. With a 3s clock, reading the correction leads to the next card timing out ('Too slow ... You played Nothing').
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/screens/Drills.tsx (arm effect deps [card, feedback, showChart, shotClockMs] ~line 836; advanceWithResult)
findings.suggestedFix: After a wrong answer in visual mode, delay arming the clock (e.g. 1.5-2 s, or until the strip is tapped), or pause the bar while a wrong-result strip is showing.

findings.title: Bone & Ink: status bar text may be unreadable (black-translucent over a cream band). Inferred, not seen on device.
findings.steps: Install to home screen on iPhone > choose Bone & Ink
findings.expected: Clock and battery are legible on every theme
findings.actual: index.html sets apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent, which on iOS means white status-bar text drawn over the page. Bone paints the top band rgb(242,236,224), so white text on cream is close to 1.1:1. theme-color is also fixed at #0d2318. I inferred this from Apple's documented behaviour; headless can't show it.
findings.suggestedFix: Check on the 13 mini. If confirmed, give Bone a darker top band behind the status bar (status-bar style can't change at runtime once installed). Also update meta theme-color in applyTheme per theme.

findings.title: One frame of Midnight Felt paints before the stored Bone theme applies on launch
findings.steps: With Bone & Ink stored, cold-load the app (no ?e2e)
findings.expected: The first painted frame already uses the stored theme
findings.actual: A requestAnimationFrame trace shows the first frame with content at t=170ms with no data-theme and body rgb(13,35,24) (dark green), then Bone at t=207ms. applyTheme runs in a useEffect after the first paint, and nothing in index.html sets it earlier. That's a dark flash on every launch for a daylight user.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the theme before React renders: a tiny inline script in index.html that reads the settings key and sets data-theme, or call applyTheme(normalizeTheme(loadSettings().theme)) in main.tsx before createRoot().render.

findings.title: Play topbar profile name is 9.5px and fails contrast in Bone (3.21:1)
findings.steps: Bone & Ink > Play tab > read the line under 'Bankroll: 100'
findings.expected: Readable secondary text (at least 12px and 4.5:1)
findings.actual: .topbar-profile-name uses inline style fontSize 0.7em and opacity 0.65, rendering at 9.52px with rgb(74,66,55) on rgb(230,220,203), which is 3.21:1. In sunlight it's effectively unreadable, and it carries the (stale) rules label.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the inline opacity, use var(--muted) at 0.75rem or larger, and move it into a CSS class so themes can tune it.

findings.title: Deck buttons in the Charts gear sheet are 30-33px wide
findings.steps: Charts > gear > Decks row
findings.expected: Tap targets at least 44px each way. The sheet has plenty of horizontal room.
findings.actual: The 1/2/6/8 segmented buttons measure 30x48, 33x48, 33x48 and 32x48 (same in WebKit). The Row order buttons are 40px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: min-width: 44px on .segmented-btn, min-height: 44px on .charts-order-btn.

findings.title: Gear icon renders as a colour emoji in WebKit and ignores the theme
findings.steps: WebKit > Charts or Drills > look at the gear button
findings.expected: A monochrome glyph tinted with the theme like the other icons (Chromium shows a dark outline gear)
findings.actual: U+2699 has no variation selector, so WebKit draws the purple-grey emoji gear on the Bone disc. That's inconsistent across themes and doesn't match the outline style elsewhere.
findings.suggestedFix: Use '⚙︎' (text presentation) or, better, an inline SVG gear with stroke currentColor.

findings.title: Charts topbar wraps both the back label and the title to two lines
findings.steps: Open Charts from Home or Settings (Chromium and WebKit, 375px)
findings.expected: A single-line topbar like Stats and Settings
findings.actual: 'Back to / Home' or 'Back to / Settings' and 'Strategy / charts' each wrap, squeezed between the gear and the mute disc. 'Back to Drills' happens to fit. The topbar height changes depending on where you came from.

narrative:
The three drills are easy to find under Drills > Keeping the count, and each step is clear on screen. Deck estimation shows a tall tray and a 4x3 answer grid. The result screen states the exact depth, the tolerance and the cards dealt, but it hides the tray, so I could not check my eye against the picture.

The True count drill is the strongest of the three. Grading always matched engine/count.ts trueCount() with floor: I checked all 14 reps in Chromium and 14 in WebKit. Fast advance with the result strip works well. A truncate slip is named exactly: "0 is truncate; your profile floors." Nowhere on the drill does it say which convention I am being graded on, though. I only found out when I got one wrong, and changing it means going Home > profile chip > Edit and scrolling halfway down the page. After switching to Round, I hit a real contradiction. +2 ÷ 4 = 0.5, I entered 0, and the strip said "Correct! +2 ÷ 4 = 0.5 → round +1". Stats then showed 13/13 correct (100%) alongside "Guessed too low 1".

Produce the true count is the realistic one, and it works, but it costs 42 s of counting per conversion, and that length can't be changed on its own screen. After OK, the next round starts flashing straight away under the result strip. My scripted counter was reading the strip and missed the first 2 cards in rounds 2 and 3, which threw its running count off by 2. A wrong-answer strip says "you entered +4 — +4 ÷ 6 = 0.67 → floor 0". The running count isn't labelled, so you can't tell whether the count, the tray read or the division went wrong.

Without ?e2e=1, a 90 ms double-tap on OK in the TC drill graded a phantom 0 against a question I never saw. It was saved as a wrong answer and replaced the strip for my real answer. In Deck estimation, double-tapping a bottom-row answer (5.0) dropped me back on the Drills list without showing the result.

Stats is where "see where I go wrong" fails. Produce TC has no section, although its history is saved. The TC section lists only the last 5 answers: after a 14-rep run all 5 were correct, so my 4 misses, including the convention slip, could not be seen. Rows don't show the right answer, and nothing counts convention slips.

WebKit rendered the TC strip, the Produce tray screen and the Deck estimation tray the same as Chromium. Conversion practice works and slips are explained one rep at a time. I'm marking the goal not achieved because a counter can't see their convention up front, can't trust the round-tie verdict or what double-taps record, and can't review their mistakes afterwards.

findings.title: Round convention on an exact half: strip says 'Correct!' above a different answer, and Stats counts it as too low
findings.steps: Profile > Edit > True count rounding: Round > Save. Open True count drill and wait for a tie, e.g. RC +2 with 4 decks left (0.5). Enter 0. Then open Stats > Drills > True count drill.

findings.title: Produce TC: the next round's cards start flashing at once, under the result you are trying to read
findings.steps: Drills > Produce the true count > Start. Count all 52 cards, enter a TC and tap OK. Read the two-line strip.
findings.expected: Time to read the verdict before the next count starts, such as a Next tap or a short 'Next round in 3…'.

My scripted counter was reading the strip and missed those cards: its running count was off by 2 in rounds 2 and 3 (it had +6 and −10 against the real +4 and −8). A miss on a new round can come from the previous round's feedback, not from counting.
findings.suggestedFix: Fast advance suits the 1-second TC drill but not a 42-second count. Eyes-on, end each round on a result view (strip plus tray with the true depth marked, plus a Next button), or show a 2 to 3 second 'Ready…' countdown before the first card.

findings.title: Deck estimation: double-tapping a bottom-row answer exits the drill or skips the result

narrative:
I played a new counter on a fresh profile. Home > Drills > Count drill was obvious. The setup screen has big targets and the default (52 cards, 800ms, Auto) starts in one tap. The first auto run (42s) shows one small card, 48x68 CSS px, in the middle of an empty 375x812 screen. I entered the count off by one and got 'Wrong. You entered 11; the running count was 10.' Nothing helps you find where it slipped. The second auto run was correct.

Switching to manual meant Back to Drills > Count drill > Options > On tap. 'Time per card 800ms' still shows even though it no longer applies. The manual run felt good: the whole screen is the tap zone and the progress hint is clear.

Checkpoints are buried under Options, below the fold. The stop screen ('CHECKPOINT / Running count so far?') is clear and leaks nothing. The read-back after a planted +2 slip that I later corrected was confusing as a user. It says 'Correct!' with 'Checkpoints: 0/2', then shows a red line 'After 47 cards: you said 1, it was 1 — expected +3, graded from your +6 at card 24 (adjusted)'. In WebKit a green line says 'you said -3, it was -2'.

Distractions ('Occasional') stopped the run 7 times in 52 cards with prompts like '-1 - (-4)' in ASCII hyphens. The result screen never mentioned them, though I got 4 of 7 wrong. The distractions landed on exactly the same cards (5, 10, 18, 25, 32, 41, 47) in a second run. Table mode looks good and reads well at 375px. But the hands are impossible (the dealer stands on 8+3 and on Q+6), the dealer row has no label, and the run is stored as '105 cards · manual · 255ms avg', a per-round gap shown as if it were card pace.

The goal failed at the last step. In Stats > Drills > Count drill the history is only the last 5 rows, all 'correct'. My early wrong run had already dropped off. There is no accuracy rate, no trend, and no way to tell which rows were auto, checkpoint, distraction or Table, so 'am I improving?' can't be answered. The only accuracy split is in Progress > Fatigue (early 67% / late 100%).

The real-timing pass showed the card element is reused between cards, so the deal-in animation plays only on card 1. Two identical cards in a row from the 2-deck shoe would look like one card. WebKit renders the same screens. The setup checkboxes there are bright white native boxes on dark green. There were no console or page errors in either engine.

findings.steps: Checkpoints: Two, On tap. At checkpoint 1 answer the true count +2. At checkpoint 2 answer the true count. Finish correctly. (WebKit: slip -1 at checkpoint 1 and carry it.)
findings.expected: A plain statement of which stretch I slipped in and by how much, e.g. 'Cards 1-24: +2 too high. Cards 25-47: dropped 2, which cancelled it. Cards 48-52: clean.'
findings.actual: 'Correct!' plus 'Checkpoints: 0/2', then a red bullet 'After 47 cards: you said 1, it was 1 — expected +3, graded from your +6 at card 24 (adjusted)'. In WebKit a green bullet says 'After 11 cards: you said -3, it was -2 — expected -3 … (adjusted)'. The grading is deliberate (#46), but a new counter sees matching numbers marked wrong and mismatched numbers marked right, and the 'expected/graded from/adjusted' wording reads as engine output.
findings.suggestedFix: Phrase each row as a stretch verdict: 'Cards 25-47: clean' or 'Cards 25-47: off by -2 (count moved -5, should have moved -3)'. Show the absolute 'you said / it was' only as secondary text, or only for the first stop.
