findings.suggestedFix: Show the Profile/CVCX block only on Play. Remember the last subtab (localStorage, try/catch) or default to the subtab with the newest data. Add a 'See history' link on the count result.

findings.title: Mid-run Back silently abandons the run, and every mode change goes through the Drills list
findings.steps: Start a 52-card On-tap run, tap 4 cards, tap Back (11px above the full-screen tap zone). Separately, from a result try to change Next card or Checkpoints.
findings.expected: Back mid-run asks first, or the run resumes. From a result, a 'Change settings' path back to this drill's setup.
findings.actual: Back drops the run (history unchanged, 7 -> 7) and lands on the Drills list. The tap zone starts at y=112, just under Back (y 54-102), so a hurried thumb can lose a run. Result Back and 'Back to Drills' both leave the drill, and Options is collapsed again on every return.
findings.suggestedFix: On the result, make the secondary action 'Change settings' (setPhase('setup')). Mid-run, have Back return to setup with a one-tap 'Leave run?' confirm, or add a guard band between the topbar and the tap zone. Remember the Options open state per screen.

findings.title: Flashed count card is tiny (48x68 CSS px) on a mostly empty phone screen
findings.steps: Count drill > Start (Cards, group 1).
findings.expected: In the core drill, the card fills a good part of the 375px width so rank and suit read at a glance (and in a car).
findings.actual: One 48x68px card in the centre with ~600px of empty space above and below. It's the same size as Play's compact layout, smaller than the Table-mode dealer cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Scale flashed cards in .count-flash-cards (e.g. transform: scale(2) or a --card-w override, ~110x155px for group 1, smaller for groups 2-3).

findings.title: Setup shows options that don't apply to the chosen mode
findings.steps: Options > Next card: On tap (Time per card 800ms still shown). Deal: Table (Count bias and Pace pressure still shown).
findings.expected: Options that don't apply are hidden or carry a note, like the existing 'Distractions are off in a timed challenge' notes.
findings.actual: Time per card stays visible and editable under On tap. In Table mode, Count bias (Neg-first/Pos-first) is offered, but start() builds makeCountTable without bias, so the choice is silently ignored.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard Time per card with !countManual (or label it 'Auto pace'). Guard Count bias with !tableOn, or apply the bias inside makeCountTable.

findings.title: Table mode deals impossible hands, and the dealer row is unlabelled
findings.steps: Deal: Table, step through 10 rounds.
findings.expected: Rounds that look like a real table: the dealer hits to 17, players don't hit soft 20, and a 'Dealer' label over the top row.
findings.actual: The dealer stands on Q♥6♥ (16) with a live player, on 8♣3♠ (11), and on 2♠A♣ (soft 13). P1 hits A♦9♠ (soft 20) and takes J♥. The top row has no label, while players have P1-P6. Hands are random by design (countTable.ts), but a new counter reads them as bugs and it undercuts 'laid out like Play'.
findings.suggestedFix: Draw the dealer to hard 17 (or the profile's S17/H17) and stop players at hard 17+/soft 19+, or at least make dealerCards satisfy dealer rules. Add a 'Dealer' label over .count-table-dealer.

findings.title: ASCII hyphen-minus in distraction prompts and count results (same family as the known peek/bet-or-sit issue)
findings.steps: Distractions: Occasional (near-count). Read the prompts and the final result.
findings.expected: A true minus sign (−) in '-1 − (−4)', 'You entered −2', 'expected −2', matching the NumPad's − key.
findings.actual: '-1 - (-4)', '-6 + (-2)', 'You entered -2; the running count was -2.', 'After 34 cards: you said -8'. The short hyphen is easy to misread at a glance, which is the whole point of a 'quick' distraction.
findings.likelyFile: src/drills/distraction.ts (prompt builder); CountDrillView.tsx formatSigned and the result-detail template
findings.suggestedFix: Route displayed signed numbers through a shared formatter that emits U+2212, in the same pass that fixes peek/bet-or-sit/pair-cancel.

findings.title: Setup controls: Group size targets 30-33px wide, labels wrap, alignment differs between rows
findings.steps: Count drill > Options at 375px.
findings.expected: 44px minimum targets, single-line segment labels, one alignment style for every row.
findings.actual: Group size buttons '1/2/3' are 30x48, 33x48 and 32x48. 'On tap', 'Neg-first', 'Pos-first' and 'Near-count' wrap onto two lines. Deal and Length rows are centred while every Options row is label-left/control-right. When scrolled, the fixed mute disc covers the top-right of the Time per card '+' stepper.
findings.suggestedFix: Set min-width: 44px on .segmented-btn and white-space: nowrap (shorten to 'Tap', 'Neg', 'Pos' if needed). Make the Deal and Length rows use the same space-between layout as the Options rows. Add scroll-padding-top or a right gutter so content doesn't scroll under the mute disc.

findings.title: WebKit (iOS) renders the setup checkboxes as bright white native boxes on the dark theme
findings.steps: Open Count drill setup in WebKit at 375x812.
findings.expected: The same dark, themed checkboxes Chromium shows.
findings.actual: Eyes-free audio, Countdown and Timed challenge show glaring white squares in WebKit; Chromium shows dark grey ones.
findings.suggestedFix: Set color-scheme: dark on :root for the dark themes, or give .count-toggle input[type=checkbox] accent-color plus a themed appearance:none style.

findings.title: Home doesn't acknowledge count practice
findings.steps: Do 8 count drill runs, then open Home.
findings.expected: Home reflects the work (e.g. 'Count drill: 7/8 correct, last run today') and the Next step adapts.
findings.actual: Home still says 'No hands played yet. Play a shoe, or start with the drills.' and Next step 'Learn basic strategy: Hard totals 0 answers'. The count work is invisible outside Stats > Drills.
findings.suggestedFix: When play stats are empty but drill history exists, show a drill summary line on Home and link it to Stats > Drills.

findings.title: OK on an empty keypad submits 0 and grades it
findings.steps: At the final count or a checkpoint, tap OK before typing.
findings.expected: OK is disabled (or asks) until a value is entered, or the display reads '0' deliberately.
findings.actual: NumPad.submit treats '' as 0 and the run is graded and recorded. A stray tap on the full-width OK ends a 52-card run as 'Wrong'.
findings.suggestedFix: Ignore OK while value === '' (show a faint 'Enter a number'). Explicitly typing 0 still submits 0.

topChanges: Make Stats > Count drill show progress: persist the mode (table, distractions, group, checkpoints) on each run, then show overall and rolling accuracy ('7/8 · last 10: 9/10'), a correct/wrong strip or sparkline over the full range, mode chips on rows, and Show all past 5 rows. Also drop the CVCX block from the Drills subtab and add a 'See history' link on the result.

Make every card visibly arrive and every interruption truly random: key flashed cards by shownIndex so card-deal-in replays (identical consecutive cards from the 2-deck shoe are currently invisible), mix the run seed into isDistractionPoint, and enlarge the flashed card from 48x68px.

Make the result screen teach: reword checkpoint rows as stretch verdicts ('Cards 25-47: off by -2'), not 'you said 1, it was 1' in red; report distraction answers (3/7); offer 'Review the cards' on a wrong run; and add a 'Change settings' button that returns to this drill's setup instead of the Drills list.

tapsOrSteps: Setup took 9 taps plus a dead end: gear, scroll, All settings (no profile link there), Back to Home, profile chip, Edit, open "Bankroll & count", tick "Vary bets with the count", Save, Play tab. The shoe took 188 taps over 46 rounds (chip, Deal, actions, 9 count-check prompts answered on the numpad, 4 insurance offers, 1 split of aces, 1 sit-out, 1 peek, 1 wrong-play Continue). End is 2 taps. Report to Stats is 1 tap on the tab bar, then 3 taps to open Accuracy by category, Mistake types and Cost of mistakes, plus Progress > Table sessions. About 205 taps in total. The automated ?e2e=1 shoe ran in 97s, about 2s per round. A non-e2e pass with real deal animation ran 10 rounds in 23s. A human would take roughly 6-8 minutes.
narrative:
I played as a counter on Chromium at 375x812, using ?e2e=1&seed=606 for the full shoe, then a 10-round pass without e2e (seed 4242), then 6 rounds in WebKit. I kept my own Hi-Lo count from the cards on the felt.

My count and the engine's agreed on every count check (13/13; the peek also matched), so the counting itself is consistent. Wrong advice did not come up: every split, double, surrender and insurance call I checked against 6D H17 DAS LS basic strategy plus the I18 was right.

Setup: the Play gear sheet has no bet-spread control. "All settings" opens a Settings screen with no way into profiles. I only found the toggle through the Home profile chip, then Edit, then the closed "Bankroll & count" section.

Play itself reads well. Chips, Deal and Sit out are obvious and every target is at least 44px. The insurance and count-check sheets dock without covering the cards. The count verdict strip shows after each check, "Shuffling…" appears, and End's two-tap arm works.

The report and Stats are where the story breaks:
- **Wong grading:** 36 of 46 rounds were marked wrong as "Play or sit out", including round 1 off a fresh shoe. With the default ramp, every TC ≤ 0 counts as "should sit out". That drags the headline down to 126/166 and Home now says my weakest area is "play or sit out".
- **Shuffle-round bet:** the bet on the round where the shuffle happened was graded against the reshuffled TC 0. I had just answered the count check correctly (+2), and nothing on screen warned that the cut card was out.
- **Stats labelling:** bet and wong errors are counted as "Basic strategy errors". Cost of mistakes calls them "index mistakes" it can't price. The Play-tab "Bet or sit" section says "No bet or sit decisions yet".
- **Peek during count check:** the peek can be held while the count check is open, and the peeked answer is graded correct.
- **Unsaved session:** reloading mid-shoe (the same thing as iOS evicting the PWA in the car) drops every graded decision, though the bankroll is kept.

WebKit rendered the bet screen, count check and report correctly; there the gear shows as an emoji and, with audio off, the second topbar row holds only End. No console or page errors in any run.

findings.title: Play-or-sit-out grading marks every round at TC <= 0 wrong, including round 1 of a fresh shoe
findings.steps: Turn on 'Vary bets with the count' with the default ramp (1u for TC<1). Play a full shoe betting the ramp exactly and sitting out only at TC -2. End.
findings.expected: Playing a neutral count at the table minimum, and above all the first hands off the top, is a normal counter decision and should not be wrong. Wong-out grading should apply only below a deliberate threshold the user chose.
findings.actual: The report shows 'Play or sit out 10/46 (22%)' and mistakes 'wong · TC +0 · you played play · correct sit-out — Wong decision at tc 0 ×16', '×18' at TC -1 and '×2' at TC -2. The headline drops to 126/166, Stats 'Your play accuracy' to 76%, and Home's coaching now reads 'weakest: play or sit out, bet sizing, hard totals'. The toggle's label says nothing about wonging.
findings.likelyFile: src/engine/game.ts (sitOutIsCorrect + the 'wong' event pushed in startRound)
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit wong-out threshold to the profile (e.g. 'Sit out at TC ≤ −1', off by default) and grade the play side only when that is set and the TC is below it. Never grade the first round after a shuffle. Until then, emit the 'play' wong event only when the user actually sat out at some point, or keep it out of the headline accuracy.

findings.title: Bet on the shuffle round is graded against the reshuffled TC 0, with no cut-card warning
findings.steps: Play the shoe to the cut card. At round 45 the count check reads 'Count ✓ +2' (TC +1, so the ramp says 2u). Bet 2 and tap Deal.
findings.expected: Either the app signals 'cut card out, shuffle next' before you bet, or the bet is graded at the count you could see.
findings.actual: Deal shuffles first, resets the running count to 0, and only then grades the bet: 'bet · TC +0 · you played 2 · correct 1 — Spread bet at tc 0'. 'Shuffling…' appears only after the bet is locked, and nothing in the discard tray or topbar marks the cut card. The same applies to the play-or-sit (wong) event.
findings.likelyFile: src/engine/game.ts (beginRound shuffles inside startRound before preDealTc is read); src/ui/screens/Table.tsx (no cut-card cue)
findings.suggestedFix: Shuffle at settle of the round that passed the cut card, not on the next Deal. Show 'Cut card — shuffling' in the message strip and reset the discard tray before the bet chips appear. The bet is then placed knowingly off the top at TC 0.

findings.title: Bet spread can't be turned on from the Play gear; 'All settings' is a dead end
findings.steps: On Play, tap the gear and scroll the Play settings sheet. Tap 'All settings' and look for profile or bet options.
findings.expected: 'Vary bets with the count' (a profile field like count-check frequency) sits in the Play sheet's 'New shoe' group, or All settings links to the profile.
findings.actual: The sheet offers Feedback, Deal speed, deviations, count checks, cut card, Losing shoe (whose note says 'graded on your bet ramp', a ramp you can't switch on from there) and bankroll. Settings has no Profiles entry. The only route is Home → 'Default (6D H17)' chip → Edit → expand 'Bankroll & count' → toggle → scroll → Save → Play tab: 9 taps after the dead end. Save gives no confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a 'Vary bets with the count' Toggle to PlaySheet's New-shoe group (held in the draft like the other profile fields, applied on close) and an 'Edit bet ramp…' link to the profile editor. Add a 'Profiles' row to Settings.

findings.title: Mid-shoe progress is lost on reload or app eviction; only End saves decisions
findings.steps: Play 8 rounds without End, then reload (the same as iOS killing the backgrounded PWA when Maps or a call takes over in the car).
findings.expected: Rounds already played are kept, either by resuming or by saving what was played as a session.
findings.actual: After reload: 'Round 0'. bjtrainer.stats.v1 has 0 sessions and no category tallies, so all 8 rounds of graded decisions are gone. The bankroll (98) is still carried, so the two disagree.
findings.likelyFile: src/ui/useGame.ts (endSession is the only saveStats call for table play)
findings.suggestedFix: Checkpoint game.events and round count to storage at each settle (or on visibilitychange/pagehide). On the next load, fold an unfinished checkpoint into stats as a session, flagged 'not ended'.

findings.title: Peek can be held while the count check is open, and the peeked answer is graded correct
findings.steps: Wait for 'Running count?'. Hold 'Hold to peek' (still visible above the sheet), read 'RC 0', type it, OK.
findings.expected: Peek is disabled while a count check is pending, or that check is marked assisted and not counted.
findings.actual: The peek shows 'RC 0 · TC 0.0 5.46 decks left' over the open numpad and the answer scores 'Count ✓ 0'. Count checks show 100% in the report; the only trace is a session-wide 'assisted — used 1 peek'.
findings.suggestedFix: Hide or disable PeekButton while game.countCheckOpen. Alternatively, if a peek happens while the check is open, grade that check as a miss/assisted and don't count it.

findings.title: Stats mislabel betting and wong mistakes as basic-strategy and index mistakes
findings.steps: After the shoe, open Stats > Play and expand Mistake types and Cost of mistakes.
findings.expected: Bet sizing and play-or-sit errors appear under their own heading, and the unpriced-mistakes note says what they are.
findings.actual: Mistake types shows 'Basic strategy errors 39': 36 wong, 2 bet and only 1 real hand error. Cost of mistakes says '39 further mistakes are counted above but not priced: index mistakes depend on the count'. None of them are index mistakes.
findings.likelyFile: src/engine/game.ts (classification 'basic-error' on bet/wong/countCheck events); src/ui/screens/Stats.tsx (unpricedMistakes copy)
findings.suggestedFix: Give bet, wong and countCheck events their own classification (e.g. 'betting', 'count'), add a 'Betting mistakes' row, and word the unpriced note by kind ('2 bet-sizing and 36 sit-out calls aren't priced').

findings.title: Stats Play tab 'Bet or sit' says 'No bet or sit decisions yet' straight after a shoe full of them
findings.steps: Play a shoe with bet spread on (45 bets, 46 play/sit decisions). Open Stats > Play and expand 'Bet or sit'.
findings.expected: The section reflects the table's bet and sit decisions, or is clearly the drill's.
findings.actual: It reads 'No bet or sit decisions yet.' because it counts only the Bet-or-sit drill, yet it is filed under the Play tab.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename it 'Bet-or-sit drill' and move it to the Drills tab, or fold the table's bet/wong tallies into it.

findings.title: Report mistake lines use jargon and bury the real hand mistake
findings.steps: End the shoe and read the Mistakes list.
findings.expected: Plain lines ordered by importance, e.g. 'TC −1: bet 8, ramp says 1' and 'K,8 v 10: hit, should stand'.
findings.actual: 'wong · TC +0 · you played play · correct sit-out — Wong decision at tc 0 ×16' comes first. The only real playing error (K,8 v 10 hit) is second, followed by 'bet · TC -1 · you played 8 · correct 1 — Spread bet at tc -1'. Raw event kinds, lowercase 'tc', and 'you played play'.
findings.suggestedFix: Give bet and wong rows their own copy (as the countCheck branch already has), and order the list as hand plays (by EV cost) first, then bets, then sit-outs.

findings.title: Split hands aren't labelled on the felt, but the results say 'Hand 1 / Hand 2'
findings.steps: Split A,A v 5 (or 8,8 v 6). Let the round settle.
findings.expected: Each split hand carries its label or result under it.
findings.actual: The strip says 'Hand 1: Push / Hand 2: Lose -2' with no label on the felt. Hand 1 is the RIGHT hand (order of play), which most people won't guess.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the hand label when game.hands.length > 1 as well, and put a W/L/P badge under each hand once settled, as bot seats already have.

findings.title: Doubled hand still shows 'Bet: 1'
findings.steps: Split 8,8 v 6, double the 8,2.
findings.expected: The doubled hand shows 2 units staked.
findings.actual: The felt keeps 'Bet: 1' under the doubled 8,2,J. hand.bet isn't changed on double; only the 'doubled' flag is set.
findings.suggestedFix: Display hand.bet * (hand.doubled ? 2 : 1), or 'Bet: 1 ×2'.

findings.title: The 'Bet cover' warning contradicts the grading
findings.steps: Bet the ramp exactly with cover bets off (the default), then End.
findings.expected: Consistent guidance.
findings.actual: A bold gold line says 'Betting that close to the count is what gets counters noticed.' The same report marks every off-ramp bet as a mistake, and nothing points to the 'Cover bets' toggle that would allow one.
findings.suggestedFix: With coverBets off, state the ratio neutrally and add 'Turn on Cover bets in your profile to practise varying it'. Reserve the warning style for when cover is on and still unused.

findings.title: Bet ramp editor shows the sentinel 'TC ≥ -99'
findings.steps: Profile editor > Bet ramp, first row.
findings.expected: 'Any count' or 'Below +1' for the floor row.
findings.actual: 'TC ≥ -99' with an ASCII hyphen and working −/+ steppers on a value that isn't a real count.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the minimum row as 'Any count' with its TC stepper hidden, and format other values with a typographic minus.

findings.title: Square tap-highlight flash on the round bet chips
findings.steps: Tap a chip in the bet row.
findings.expected: No rectangle behind a circular chip.
findings.actual: A teal square shows behind the round '1' chip on tap (no -webkit-tap-highlight-color on .chip-btn; iOS draws its grey rounded rect the same way).
findings.suggestedFix: Add -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent and an :active scale/brightness state to .chip-btn.

findings.title: Sitting out on a solo table shows only the dealer's up card
findings.steps: Tap 'Sit out' at TC -2.
findings.expected: Something to back-count while sitting out.
findings.actual: One up card plus a face-down card that is never turned. The round passes with one countable card; the hole card leaves the shoe unseen. The count stays consistent because the engine doesn't count it.
findings.suggestedFix: On a sit-out, deal a phantom seat or reveal the hole card and play the dealer out, so the user practises watching cards while sitting out.

topChanges: Fix the grading that poisons the report: grade play-or-sit only against an explicit, opt-in wong-out threshold (never off the top), and shuffle on the settle of the cut-card round with a visible 'Cut card — shuffling' cue, so the next bet is graded at the count the user could see.
Put 'Vary bets with the count' (and a link to the bet ramp) in the Play gear sheet, and add a Profiles row to Settings so 'All settings' isn't a dead end.

Make Play's results trustworthy and durable: checkpoint graded events each round so a reload or iOS eviction doesn't erase the shoe, disable peek while a count check is open, and give bet/wong mistakes their own classification, copy and Stats rows (Mistake types, Cost of mistakes note, the Play-tab 'Bet or sit' section).

tapsOrSteps: Getting into the drill took 1 tap (Home Next step "Start" opens Flashcards with the first card already dealt). After that, nothing in the app tells you that you've learned basic strategy until Home's Next step changes from "Learn basic strategy" to "Mastery sweep". In a measured fresh run with no ?e2e=1, that took about 1,190 graded answers. The run was: 420 answers from a simulated beginner who guesses and then remembers every correction cell by cell, followed by 770 perfect answers checked against the engine (0 graded wrong, so the app's grading agrees with src/engine/strategy.ts basicPlay). After 1,070 answers, the last 650 of them perfect, Home still said "Pairs are at 89%; get every category to 90%". At a believable beginner pace of 3-4 s per answer that is roughly 60-80 minutes, not 10. After 10 real minutes (about 150-200 answers) the user is still at "Soft totals are at 68%", and nothing on screen shows progress. 47 screenshots are in C:/Users/jackp/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-jackp/5eb9dd98-f8da-490b-a046-a394be7c9a16/scratchpad/swarmB/s01-first-run/shots/. Console and page errors: none, in Chromium or WebKit.
narrative:
I played a new user who knows the rules but no strategy, starting from a clean install at 375x812 in Chromium (mobile, touch). Home is tidy, but the most eye-catching button is the gold "Play a shoe". The Next step card's "Start" is styled as a secondary button, even though the card is the one telling me to "Learn basic strategy". The card's reason ("Hard totals: 0 answers so far, 20 needed to judge") reads like a gate, not an instruction. "0/17 indices seen" and "Default (6D H17)" mean nothing to a beginner.

Tapping Start drops you straight into a Flashcards quiz. Nothing teaches first: no look at the chart, no "this is how it works", no hand total on screen, and no progress counter. Answering is fast and the feedback is clear about *what*: a green "Correct! K,9 v 6 — Stand", or a red strip with "You played Split / Right play Stand". It never says *why*. The copy just repeats itself ("Basic strategy error. Basic stand vs dealer 3"). Sometimes it uses jargon a beginner has never met: "Phantom deviation" on 12 v 2/3 stands, 6,6 v 2/3 and 5,5 v A. "Next review: now" is puzzling, including right after a correct answer.

"Show on chart" is the best learning moment. It opens the full chart (correct for 6D H17 DAS LS; I checked every cell against standard strategy and against src/engine) with the right cell highlighted, and "Back to hand" returns cleanly. The "Wrong tap" link is a trap for this user, though. It looks like "explain this", but it erases the correction ("Not counted: A,5 v 2") so the lesson is lost.

Back from Flashcards goes to the Drills menu, not Home. That menu leads with five card-counting drills, and Flashcards sits below the fold.

The core failure is the gate. It compares lifetime accuracy per category with 90%, so every mistake made while learning stays in the denominator for good. A learner who has fully learned the chart still sees "Pairs are at 89%" after hundreds of perfect answers. And Start always reopens "All" hands, even when the card names Soft totals or Pairs.

When the gate finally cleared, the next step was a 330-card Mastery sweep with a progress counter (0 / 330 cleared). Flashcards never had a counter like that.

WebKit (Home, wrong strip, Show on chart) matched Chromium except for one thing: the ⚙ on Home's Settings button renders as a colour emoji there. Charts/Stats: the Charts tab top bar wraps "Back to Home" and "Strategy charts" onto two lines each. Stats opens on Play/CVCX rows that show only dashes for a drills-only beginner.

findings.title: 'Learn basic strategy' gate uses lifetime accuracy, so learners stay stuck long after they know the chart
findings.steps: Fresh install -> Home Start -> answer as a beginner who learns from each correction (420 answers, about 15% wrong while learning) -> then answer 650 in a row perfectly -> Home
findings.expected: Once recent play is at 90%+, Home moves on (or at least shows progress toward it). The story's 10-minute goal should be reachable for someone who has learned the chart.
findings.actual: After 1,070 answers (last 650 perfect) Home still says 'Learn basic strategy — Pairs are at 89%; get every category to 90%.' It cleared only at about 1,190 answers (roughly 60-80 min at human pace). At 10 minutes it said 'Soft totals are at 68%'. Mistakes made while learning are never forgotten.
findings.suggestedFix: Judge each category on a recent window (e.g. the last 20-30 answers per category, or per-cell last-N via cellStats.lastAt) instead of summed lifetime right/wrong. Keep MIN_CATEGORY_ANSWERS as the minimum sample. Show the windowed figure in the 'why' line.

findings.title: 'Learn basic strategy' quizzes from the first second; there is no learn/study step and no explanation of why
findings.steps: Fresh install -> Home Next step 'Learn basic strategy' -> Start
findings.expected: A brand-new user is shown the chart or a short primer first (or a 'study the chart' option), and wrong answers explain the rule (e.g. 'Always split 2s and 3s against 2-7').
findings.actual: The first card is already dealt with no instructions. Wrong feedback only repeats the answer: 'Basic strategy error. Basic split vs dealer 3'. The chart is only reachable by making a mistake (Show on chart) or by leaving for the Charts tab. That means a beginner can only learn by trial and error, which (with the lifetime gate) keeps failing them.
findings.suggestedFix: On the first flash launch with no cellStats, show a one-screen 'How to read the chart' plus the chart (with a 'Start quiz' button), or add a 'Study chart' button to the Next step card. Add a one-line rule per region to the wrong strip (from the cell's row/column group) in place of the duplicated 'Basic X vs dealer N' text.

findings.title: Flashcards shows no progress toward the goal Home set
findings.steps: Home says '20 needed to judge… get every category to 90%' -> Start -> answer cards
findings.expected: A visible counter or meter in Flashcards, like Mastery's '0 / 330 cleared' (e.g. 'Soft 6/20 · Pairs 58%').
findings.actual: Nothing in Flashcards shows count, accuracy or distance to the goal. The only way to check is Back -> Home tab, which also loses your place in the drill flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a slim status line under the scope chips with per-category answers and accuracy (the same figures nextStep uses), and a toast when the Home goal is met.

findings.title: Next step names a weak category but Start opens 'All' hands
findings.steps: With soft or pairs the weakest, Home says 'Soft totals are at 68%' (or 'Pairs are at 73%') -> Start
findings.expected: Flashcards opens scoped to Soft (or Pairs), the category the card just named.
findings.actual: It always opens on 'All' (aria-pressed All:true), so most cards are hard totals the user has already mastered. drillLaunch only carries the mode.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend DrillLaunch with an optional scope ('hard'|'soft'|'pair') that nextStep fills from the thin/low category, and apply it in Drills when launch==='flash'.

findings.title: 'Wrong tap' erases the correction a beginner needs
findings.steps: Flashcards -> answer wrong (A,5 v 2 Stand) -> tap 'Wrong tap' at the top right of the red strip
findings.expected: Either the label makes clear it means 'I mis-tapped, don't count it', or the right play stays visible after pressing it.
findings.actual: The strip collapses to 'Not counted: A,5 v 2'. The 'Right play Hit' line and 'Show on chart' disappear and the miss isn't recorded. A beginner reading 'Wrong tap' as 'why was this wrong?' loses the lesson and nothing gets re-queued.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to 'Mis-tap, don't count' (or 'Undo: mis-tap'), and keep 'Right play X' visible in the 'Not counted' strip.

findings.title: Plain flashcards label beginner mistakes 'Phantom deviation'
findings.steps: Flashcards (no count shown) -> 7,5 v 3 Stand, or 9,3 v 2 Stand, or 6,6 v 2 Stand, or 5,5 v A Double
findings.expected: 'Basic strategy error' (no count is involved in a plain flashcard), or plain words a beginner can follow.
findings.actual: 'Phantom deviation. Basic hit vs dealer 3'. The beginner never deviated and has never heard of indices.
findings.suggestedFix: When the card has no tc (plain flashcard, deck Chart), classify every miss as basic-strategy-error. Keep phantom-deviation for With count, Mixed, Play and the quiz.

findings.title: Back from a Home-launched drill goes to the Drills menu, which leads with counting drills
findings.steps: Home -> Start -> Flashcards -> Back
findings.expected: Back returns to Home (where the user came from), or the Drills menu puts 'Knowing the plays' first for a basic-strategy learner.
findings.actual: It lands on the Drills picker, where 'Keeping the count' (5 counting drills) fills the screen and Flashcards is below the fold.
findings.suggestedFix: When mode came from takeDrillLaunch(), make onBack call onNavigate('home'). Consider ordering the picker sections Plays -> Count -> Pressure.

findings.title: Home's visual hierarchy favours 'Play a shoe' over the recommended Next step
findings.steps: Fresh install -> Home
findings.expected: The recommended action (Next step Start) is the primary, most prominent button.
findings.actual: 'Play a shoe' is the gold primary button, while Start is a muted secondary button inside the card. A beginner told to 'learn basic strategy' is drawn to the table.
findings.suggestedFix: Make next-step-btn u-btn-primary and demote 'Play a shoe' to secondary until the next step is 'play'.

findings.title: Home 'weakest' line lists every category, including ones at 94%
findings.steps: After about 120 answers -> Home
findings.expected: Only the categories that are actually below target.
findings.actual: 'weakest: soft totals, pairs, hard totals' with hard at 94%. weakestCategories only filters out pct < 1 and lists up to 3.
findings.suggestedFix: Filter to pct < CATEGORY_TARGET (0.9), or show just the single weakest category with its %.

findings.title: Beginner-facing jargon with no explanation (Next review: now, Surrender OK / No surrender, indices, 6D H17, CVCX)
findings.steps: Home and Flashcards on first run, then Stats
findings.expected: Short plain-language hints or hidden-until-relevant labels for a new user.
findings.actual: 'Next review: now' even after a correct answer. The 'Surrender OK' / 'No surrender' pill changes per card with no explanation. Home shows '0/17 INDICES SEEN' and 'Default (6D H17)'. Stats opens on the Play tab with four CVCX rows of dashes, and Options shows Fallbacks / With count with no description.
findings.suggestedFix: Hide 'Next review' unless it is later than now. Add a title or first-time hint to the surrender pill. Hide the indices stat until the deviation step. Default Stats to Drills or Progress when there are no Play rounds.

findings.title: Settings gear renders as a colour emoji on WebKit/iOS
findings.steps: WebKit 375x812 -> Home
findings.expected: A monochrome glyph matching Chromium and the rest of the UI.
findings.actual: ⚙ renders as a grey/purple emoji next to 'Settings'.
findings.suggestedFix: Append U+FE0E ('⚙︎ ') or use the inline SVG gear the tab gear buttons use.

findings.title: Charts tab top bar wraps onto two lines
findings.steps: Home -> Charts tab
findings.expected: A single-line top bar like the other tabs.
findings.actual: 'Back to Home' and 'Strategy charts' both wrap to two lines next to the gear and the mute disc. 'Back to Home' is also redundant on a tab screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a short 'Back' label (or drop it when Charts was opened from the tab bar), and keep the title on one line with nowrap and ellipsis.

topChanges: Judge 'Learn basic strategy' on a recent window per category (e.g. last 20-30 answers) instead of lifetime totals, so a learner who has the chart down clears it within minutes, not after about 1,200 answers (nextStep.ts).

Add a learn step: show the chart and a one-screen 'how to read it' on the first flash launch, and give wrong answers a one-line rule (why), not the duplicated 'Basic X vs dealer N'. Never call a plain-flashcard miss a 'Phantom deviation'.

Make Start focus on, and show progress toward, the stated goal: pass the weak category as the Flashcards scope, add a per-category counter/meter to Flashcards with a 'goal met' toast, and make Start the primary Home button.

tapsOrSteps: Making the profile active took 11 taps: the profile chip on Home, New profile, the name field (typing), Decks 2, S17, Late surrender off, a scroll, Save, tapping the new profile's row to make it active, and Back to Home. Switching back to Default took 3 taps: chip, Default row, Back. Checking everything (Charts plus an index cell, Flashcards with about 18 cards, a Custom deck of 10 cells, the Deviation quiz, 5-8 Play rounds, the Play gear sheet, End twice) brought the full runs to 48 taps (Chromium e2e phase 1), 59 taps (phase 2) and 51 taps (WebKit). The automated time was about 36 s with ?e2e=1 and about 76 s plus 90 s with real timings. A real person would take roughly 6-8 minutes. Screenshots are in C:/Users/jackp/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-jackp/5eb9dd98-f8da-490b-a046-a394be7c9a16/scratchpad/swarmB/s08-house-rules-profile/shots/: A* = Chromium e2e phase 1, B* = phase 2 and switch back, R*/S* = real timings, Aw* = WebKit, Q* = Deviation quiz probe. There are 150+ in total and the key ones were read.
narrative:
Overall the profile works: the new rules reach every surface tested, and switching back to Default leaks nothing in the rules themselves. The exceptions are the drill history, and two doubling indexes that conflict with the 2-deck chart and get graded against the player in the quiz.

Home only shows the profile as a chip, "Default (6D H17)", which opens Profiles. Profiles has New profile, and the form is clear: Decks 2, S17, untick Late surrender. The cut card resets itself to "0.5 decks behind, 2-deck shoe", and Surrender indices greys out with "Needs late surrender, which is off in this profile's rules". Save is at the bottom of a long form (about 2400px). After Save, the list shows the new row, but the profile is NOT made active and there is no rules summary on the row. To switch you have to know to tap the row's name, which looks like a label. Once you do, the Home chip and the Play topbar show "Local 2D S17".

Charts shows "2 deck · S17 · DAS · No surrender". I compared all 350 rendered cells against src/engine/charts/d2_s17.ts with no-surrender applied: zero mismatches. That includes 9v2 Dh, 15/16 v 10 H, 16vA H, A7v2 S, A8v6 S, 6,6v7 P and 7,7v8 P. The Custom painter showed the same codes.

Flashcards always showed the "No surrender" chip and Surrender was greyed out. All 18 random cards and a 14-card Custom deck of the cells that differ were graded to the 2-deck S17 rules; I checked each answer against src/engine/strategy.ts correctPlay. Playing the Default answer (A,8 v 6 Double, A,7 v 2 Double) was marked Wrong with "Right play Stand".

Play dealt a 2-deck shoe (the discard tray has 1 tick), Surrender was disabled, and the gear sheet says "Saved to the Local 2D S17 profile" with the 2-deck cut card.

The Indexes list follows S17 (16v9 +5, 10vA +4, 12v6 -2, 11vA +1). But it carries 11vA and 9v2 "double at TC >= +1", which the 2-deck chart already doubles at every count. The Deviation quiz then marks "hit at TC -1 / TC 0" wrong while quoting "double at TC >= +1" as the reason.

Switching back to Default:
- The Home chip, the Charts summary and every chart cell match the earlier capture exactly.
- Default's stored rules are byte-identical, and each profile has its own bankroll.
- The Custom grid shows Rh/Rs/Ds again, Flashcards shows "Surrender OK" on surrenderable hard hands and grades 9,6 v 10 as Surrender, and Play deals 6 decks (5 ticks).

Shared state does leak, though. The Flashcards spaced-repetition (SR) schedule (bjtrainer.flashsr.v1) and the per-cell stats are keyed by cell alone. Hard 17 v A, answered "Stand" under the 2-deck profile, sits in box 1 due tomorrow under Default, where the right play is Surrender. Home accuracy (95%, 44 decisions) mixes both rule sets.

There were no console or page errors in any Chromium or WebKit run. WebKit matched Chromium apart from a serif font in the profile name field.

findings.title: Deviation quiz contradicts itself on 11vA and 9v2 under 2-deck rules
findings.steps: Make a 2D S17 DAS no-surrender profile and make it active. Drills > Deviation quiz > Index '9 v 2: double at TC ≥ +1'. A card comes up at TC +0 (or choose '11 v A' and get TC -1). Answer Hit, as the index label says.
findings.expected: For 2 decks, where basic strategy already doubles 9v2 and 11vA, these indexes should be dropped (or replaced with a correct 2-deck index). The quiz should never grade against the very rule it is quoting.
findings.actual: It shows 'Wrong 2,7 v 2 at TC +0. You played Hit, Right play Double. Basic strategy error. 9 v 2: double at TC ≥ +1', and the same for 11 v A at TC -1. Charts > Indexes lists both, with corner marks on cells that already say Dh, so the player is taught to hit below +1.
findings.suggestedFix: In indexSetFor, when decks <= 2, remove (or swap for the correct 2-deck version) any index whose action the base chart already plays at TC 0: 11vA and 9v2 for 2D, and the equivalents for 1D. Add a unit test: for every chart and index set, no gte index may name the chart's own action. The indexes are 6-deck numbers, so the Indexes header could also say so for 1-2 decks.

findings.title: Drill history is shared across profiles with different correct answers
findings.steps: Under the 2-deck no-surrender profile, answer hard 17 v A 'Stand' (or 16 v 10 'Stand') in Flashcards. Switch to Default (6D H17 LS). Read localStorage bjtrainer.flashsr.v1, or look at Home accuracy.
findings.expected: Learning state for a cell whose correct play depends on the rules should be kept per profile (or per rules set), or at least reset or flagged when the answer differs.
findings.actual: bjtrainer.flashsr.v1['hard-17-v-A'] = {box:1, reviews:1, due tomorrow} under Default, whose right play is Rs (surrender). The schedule pushes back a cell the player has never answered correctly under these rules. Home shows '95% accuracy, 44 decisions' mixed from both rule sets, even though Stats says 'Profile: Default (6D H17)'.
findings.suggestedFix: Key the SR deck and per-cell tallies by a rules signature (deck class, s17, das, ls), or store the expected action alongside each entry and treat a changed expected action as a fresh card.

findings.title: A new profile isn't made active on Save, and the way to activate it is hidden
findings.steps: Profiles > New profile > set the rules > Save.
findings.expected: Saving a new profile offers to use it (or just makes it active), and each row shows its rules.
findings.actual: You land back on the list with Default still 'Active'. The only way to switch is to tap the profile's name text, which looks like a label, not a button. Rows show only the name, so 'Local 2D S17' versus a profile called 'Vegas' gives no hint of decks or surrender.
findings.suggestedFix: On saving a new profile, call selectActive(cleaned.id), or show 'Use this profile' as a button. Add a second line to each row with rulesetSummary(p.rules), and a visible 'Use' button or radio on rows that aren't active.

findings.title: Drills and Play never say which rules are in force
findings.steps: Make the 2-deck profile active and open Flashcards, Deviation quiz or Play.
findings.expected: A short rules line (e.g. '2D · S17 · DAS · No surr') or the profile chip is visible, so you can confirm you're drilling your casino's game.
findings.actual: Flashcards and the quiz show only a 'No surrender' chip. Play shows only the name the user chose ('Local 2D S17'). Charts is the only screen that states the rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Put rulesetSummary(activeProfile.rules) next to the RulesChip in the drill views and under the profile name in the Play topbar.

findings.title: Last answer's correction appears next to the new card's 'No surrender' chip
findings.steps: Default profile: in Flashcards, answer 9,6 v 10 with Hit. The app auto-advances to a soft or pair hand.
findings.expected: The correction is clearly about the previous hand.
findings.actual: The red strip says 'Right play Surrender' directly under a 'No surrender' chip that belongs to the new card. A glance reads as a contradiction.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the strip 'Last hand', or hide or dim the chip while a strip from a previous card is showing.

findings.title: Home 'Indices seen' total is always the H17 set
findings.steps: Make the S17 profile active and look at Home. Then look at Charts > Indexes.
findings.expected: The denominator matches the active profile's index set (18 under S17).
findings.actual: Home shows 0/17. Charts lists 18 (11vA is active under S17), and 11vA progress can never count.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass strategyRulesFor(activeProfile) to readiness() and use indexSetFor(rules).filter(active).

findings.title: Deck-count segment buttons are 30-33px wide
findings.steps: Profiles > New profile > Rules > Decks 1/2/6/8.
findings.expected: Tap targets of at least 44px.
findings.actual: Measured 30x48, 33x48, 33x48 and 32x48. On a 375px phone it's easy to hit 1 when you meant 2.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the segmented buttons min-width: 44px. The row has room.

findings.title: Profile name field ignores the app font (serif in WebKit)
findings.steps: Open Profiles > New profile in WebKit.
findings.expected: The input uses the app's sans-serif font.
findings.actual: 'Local 2D S17' renders in Times. app.css sets font-family: inherit on button only, not on input.
findings.suggestedFix: Add font: inherit to input, select and textarea globally (or to the profile input classes).

findings.title: ASCII hyphen in the Deviation quiz TC and its correction ('TC -1')
findings.steps: Deviation quiz, any card at a negative count.
findings.expected: A true minus sign, matching the index labels ('TC ≤ −2').
findings.actual: The big 'TC -1' readout and 'at TC -1' in the correction use a hyphen-minus. This may share a root with the known peek/bet-or-sit hyphen issue, but it's a different screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Use U+2212 in formatSigned.

findings.title: Rules summary says '2 deck' instead of '2 decks'
findings.steps: Charts with the 2-deck profile active.
findings.expected: '2 decks' (or '2D').
findings.actual: '2 deck · S17 · DAS · No surrender'.
findings.suggestedFix: Pluralise when decks > 1, or use '2D'.

topChanges: Fix the index set per deck count: drop or correct 11vA and 9v2 for 1-2 decks, where basic strategy already doubles, so Charts > Indexes, the corner marks and the Deviation quiz stop teaching the player to hit and then marking it wrong.

Keep the spaced-repetition (SR) schedule and per-cell stats per rules set (or reset a cell when its correct action changes), so drilling one casino's rules doesn't mark cells as learned under another profile.

After saving a new profile, make it active (or show a 'Use this profile' button), and show rulesetSummary on each profile row and on the drill and Play screens, so the player can see which rules they are training on.
